subject: anatomy
title: Mixed practice anatomy: high-yield rapid review

steps.tx: Rapid anatomy review covers several high-yield facts. The **pudendal nerve** arises from S2, S3 and S4, and blocking it gives perineal analgesia without relieving labour pain from the uterine segment. The **Allen's test** checks the integrity of the palmar arch by compressing both arteries at the wrist and watching fingers refill. A normal return of colour within about 5 seconds is reassuring.

vis.alt: Stepwise clinical protocol for the modified Allen test evaluating collateral arterial perfusion via the superficial and deep palmar arches prior to radial artery cannulation or puncture.
vis.caption: Modified Allen's test: palmar flushing within 5 to 7 seconds confirms ulnar collateral patency before radial cannulation.

steps.tx: Trachea and bronchi show a clear age pattern. In children the **tracheal bifurcation** lies at T3, while in adults it sits at T4 to T5. The trachea runs from the lower border of the cricoid cartilage, at C6, down to the upper border of T5 in adults. Narrow paediatric airways offer more resistance, so infection causes distress more easily.

steps.tx: Collagen types are frequently tested. **Type I collagen** is the main form in bone, tendon, ligament, skin and cornea, and it makes up most of the unmineralised bone matrix. **Type IV collagen** forms sheets in the basement membrane. Type II is found in cartilage and the vitreous, while type III is found in reticular fibres and blood vessel walls.

steps.tx: Chromosome and nerve structure questions are common. A **metacentric chromosome** has its centromere exactly in the middle, and chromosome 21 is **acrocentric**, with the centromere near one end. **Female sex chromatin** (Barr body) is present in XX cells and absent in XO, while XXX cells have more than one. Mitosis studies for karyotyping are usually done at metaphase.

steps.tx: Abdominal vessels and organs are common exam targets. The **middle colic artery** runs in the transverse mesocolon, and the **inferior mesenteric artery** is the least likely vessel to cause major damage when injured, because the marginal artery usually sustains the colon. The pancreas is retroperitoneal and does not move with respiration. Retrocaval ureter results from abnormal development of the IVC, with a persistent right posterior subcardinal vein.
